scopeStatement: This reconstruction covers the 111.061-second tutorial, its complete 32-cue SRT, all probed visual/UI/OCR carriers, the observable operations and before/during/after transitions, and the AAC stereo track. It distinguishes author claims from visible state; pre-existing files from agent changes; external art generation and human file handling from coding-agent work; and a local index.html browser SPA preview from a shipped mobile, hosted, or standalone game. Secrets, external image-tool identity/settings, cross-cut project continuity, exact elapsed development time, and unoperated functionality remain unknown.

viewerChange.from: A viewer may initially understand the video as a fully automatic, three-hour, zero-code AI game build.
viewerChange.to: The evidence supports a narrower workflow: install/configure Claude Code with Kimi K2, supply a detailed prewritten specification and already populated project materials, fill an art gap in a separate image UI, manually save/name/place files, hand them to the coding agent, inspect a local browser SPA, and ask for a CSS/layout revision. Several headline claims remain unverified.
viewerChange.practicalOutcome: The viewer can reproduce the shown setup and handoff sequence while preserving human ownership, provenance boundaries, local-runtime limits, and untested/unknown claims.

knowledgeUnits.title: Human retains workflow ownership
knowledgeUnits.statement: The demonstrated process is human-directed: the author supplies/curates a detailed specification, chooses to proceed, creates or obtains the API key, handles external image generation and local files, reviews dialogue line by line, rejects a layout, and formulates the revision. The coding agent performs configuration-dependent generation/integration/editing inside those human decisions. Describing the workflow as autonomous end-to-end generation would erase necessary inputs and review gates.

Across independent stages, those observable actions justify the inference that the human retains workflow ownership.
